Each raffle is an EIP-1167 minimal-proxy clone of one shared implementation (e.g. OpenZeppelin Clones), not a contract deployed with `new` or an upgradeable proxy.

The factory's implementation address cannot change after deployment, and the implementation's code cannot change or be destroyed (no selfdestruct, no delegatecall to a mutable target), so every clone permanently runs the same logic.
The entry price is exactly 1,000,000 raw quote-token units, and buying N entries pulls exactly N x 1,000,000 units from the buyer.

The configured quote token is the official USDC contract on the target chain (Ethereum per sentence 1), not just any 6-decimal token. Only partly enforceable on-chain, because code cannot prove token identity, so it rests on deployment configuration.
The configured quote token reports decimals() == 6 (enforced at construction or by deployment), and all amounts are raw 6-decimal units, so 1,000,000 units = 1 USDC.

requirements.quote: One purchase mints a transferable ERC721 ticket
requirements.checkable: Every successful purchase call mints exactly one new ERC-721 ticket to the recipient, whatever the number of entries bought.

requirements.quote: ticket representing a contiguous inclusive range
requirements.checkable: Each ticket records the entries [previousTotal+1, previousTotal+entryCount]; ranges across tickets are gapless and non-overlapping, so every entry 1..totalEntries belongs to exactly one ticket.
Both endpoints belong to the ticket: its entry count is lastEntry - firstEntry + 1 (e.g. for refunds), and it wins iff firstEntry <= winningEntry <= lastEntry.
Each raffle escrows exactly one ERC-721 token (one prize contract and one tokenId); non-ERC-721 prizes are rejected, and no second prize can be deposited or accounted for.
